title: Security & Compliance PRD: Enterprise SSO, RBAC, Audit Logging, KMS/HSM (scope, acceptance, sign-off)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: This PRD defines the minimum viable security and compliance surface required for our Private and Dedicated offerings: enterprise SSO (SAML 2.0 + SCIM provisioning), role-based access control (RBAC) with admin UX, immutable and exportable audit logs, and customer-managed key integration (KMS + optional HSM). Goals: 1) Allow enterprise customers to delegate authentication and provisioning to their IdP (Okta, ADFS, Azure AD) via SAML and SCIM v2. 2) Provide a flexible RBAC model mapping to organization/team/route-level permissions with UI and API management. 3) Ship auditable, tamper-evident logs with configurable retention and export hooks to SIEM. 4) Enable encryption key management integrations: hosted AWS KMS for Redwood-managed keys, and BYOK/HSM options for Private deployments. Non-goals (v1): full OIDC authorization code flows for application-level OAuth (deferred), advanced attribute-based access controls (ABAC) beyond role mapping, and cross-tenant single sign-on. Stakeholders: PM (Aisha Patel), Security/InfoSec (Lena Cho), Eng Leads (Ravi Menon, Carlos Vega), UX (Mia Torres), SRE (Ben Hall), Legal/Compliance (Sofia Alvarez). Constraints: timeline (ship core in Q1 private-2025), compatibility with existing runtime and KV caching behavior, privacy/legal requirements for audit retention per customer region (EU/US).
acceptance_criteria: SSO: Support SAML 2.0 SP integration including metadata upload, IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows, and metadata validation checks.
SCIM: Support SCIM v2 provisioning endpoints for user/group create/update/delete with configurable mapping and a test provisioning UI in Console.
RBAC: Implement role model with four baseline roles (Org Admin, Project Admin, Contributor, Viewer) and API endpoints to create custom roles; RBAC enforced across Console and REST/SDK admin APIs.
Attribute mapping: Allow mapping of SAML attributes (email, name, groups) into user profile and roles; fallback to SCIM group sync when available.

Audit logs: All admin-level actions (auth config changes, role grants/revokes, key rotation, deployment upgrades) are recorded to append-only audit logs with timestamp, actor, and diff; logs are exportable via API and streamable to customer SIEM (syslog/HTTPS).
Tamper evidence: Audit logs deployed with append-only storage and cryptographic signing for Private deployments; hosted option uses internal tamper-evidence controls and can export signed bundles.
Retention: Console allows per-tenant retention settings with defaults (90 days) and options (30/90/365) with export before deletion; retention policy honored in both hosted and private modes.

KMS integration: Support AWS KMS for hosted keys; support customer-managed KMS via external key IDs for Private; provide documented key rotation procedure and API to trigger rotation; no plaintext key material is ever stored in Redwood control plane.
HSM/BYOK: For Private deployments, support integration points for HSM (PKCS#11) with instructions for key provisioning and zero-downtime rotation where supported by the customer's HSM.
Console UX: Admin flows for SSO setup, SCIM testing, role management and audit log searching exist and pass usability validation from Design.
APIs and SDKs: Admin endpoints for SSO config, RBAC management, and audit export are available with docs and examples; SDKs updated for common languages.
E2E tests: Automated end-to-end tests for SAML login, SCIM provisioning, RBAC enforcement, log generation and export, and KMS key rotation exist in CI with green results.
Backward compatibility: Existing tenants without SSO remain unaffected; adding SSO must not break API tokens or service accounts until explicitly revoked.
Compliance artifacts: Required documentation (runbook, threat model addendum, SOC2 control mapping) produced and added to compliance folder before sign-off.

open_questions: Which SAML attributes will be required by default vs. optional for provisioning? (email required, groups optional)
Default audit log retention for customers with strict data residency requirements (EU-only tenants)?
Will we enforce MFA or just relay IdP policies for SSO sessions?
Clarify exact RBAC granularity required by top 3 enterprise customers in pipeline
Cost model for long-term audit storage for hosted vs. private tenants
decisions: Adopt SAML 2.0 + SCIM v2 as initial supported standards; OIDC deferred to backlog.
RBAC model will be role-based (Org/Project/Route) with custom role creation rather than full ABAC in v1.
Audit logs will be append-only and exportable; cryptographic signing required for Private installs.
KMS strategy: hosted -> managed AWS KMS; private -> BYOK with HSM integration option.
Design will provide a single admin UX for SSO/SCIM setup with an advanced JSON editor for edge cases.

acceptance_test_plan: Test 1: Configure SAML IdP with test metadata -> perform IdP-initiated and SP-initiated login; expected: user session established and user attributes populated.
Test 2: Push user/group changes via SCIM -> expect users created/updated/deactivated in Console within TTL and role assignments applied.
Test 3: Grant and revoke roles via API -> expect immediate permission changes enforced on subsequent API calls.
Test 4: Trigger admin action (key rotation) -> audit record generated with actor and diff; exportable via API and present in Console search.
Test 5: KMS rotation using customer key -> rotation succeeds without downtime for in-flight requests (where HSM supports hot-rotation); otherwise clear warning presented.
implementation_notes: Eng spike required to validate SAML libraries for Rust/Go runtime and Console; prefer well-maintained OSS implementations.
Audit logs storage for hosted will use append-only S3 buckets with server-side signing; private will rely on customer-provided storage or embedded signing keys.
Ensure SCIM endpoints are rate-limited and idempotent; record provisioning failures to admin dashboard.
Provide migration guide for existing tenants that currently use API keys only; include step to set SSO as primary auth and create service accounts if needed.
Coordinate with Ops for upgrade steps in Dedicated clusters to install KMS connectors and HSM drivers for Private customers.
